findings.description: The inline policy grants wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on all resources ("Resource": "*"), violating least privilege and allowing the IAM user to perform virtually any operation across these services.

A static IAM access key/secret is generated for the user and will be persisted in plaintext within Terraform state; combined with the excessively permissive policy attached to the same user, compromise of this key/state grants broad account access.
The access key secret material is exposed via a Terraform output without being marked 'sensitive', risking disclosure of credentials in CLI output, logs, or CI pipeline artifacts.

Granting permissions via an inline policy directly on an individual IAM user (rather than through a role or group) bypasses centralized access control management and increases risk of privilege drift and escalation.
